blocks.title: Planning a welcome lunch in Gatineau
blocks.context: Lucie, a volunteer, asks Raj and Mei what they like, to plan Friday's lunch for newcomers.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Pour le dîner de vendredi, à midi, j'ai une question. Qu'est-ce que vous aimez ?
lines.en: Hello! For Friday's lunch (le dîner, in Québec), at noon, I have a question. What do you like?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Moi, j'aime le poulet et le riz. Mais je n'aime pas le poisson.
lines.en: I like chicken and rice. But I don't like fish.

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: J'aime beaucoup les légumes et les fruits. Je n'aime pas la viande : je suis végétarienne.
lines.en: I really like vegetables and fruit. I don't like meat: I'm vegetarian.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.fr: Et le fromage ? Tu aimes le fromage ?
lines.en: And cheese? Do you like cheese?

lines.speaker: Mei
lines.fr: Oui ! J'aime le fromage et le pain.
lines.en: Yes! I like cheese and bread.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Et moi, j'aime le café, mais pas le thé.
lines.en: And I like coffee, but not tea.

lines.speaker: Lucie
lines.en: Perfect! Thank you, Raj. Thank you, Mei!

blocks.title: Three meals a day (in France)
blocks.fr:
Le matin, à sept heures, c'est le petit-déjeuner.
À midi, c'est le déjeuner.
Le soir, à vingt heures, c'est le dîner.
blocks.en:
In the morning, at seven o'clock, it's breakfast.
At noon, it's lunch.
In the evening, at 8 p.m., it's dinner.

blocks.body:
Listen first and spot the food words. Notice that every food word comes with a little word in front of it: [[le]], [[la]], [[l']] or [[les]].

Did you notice? Lucie says [[le dîner]]… [[à midi]]. In Québec, [[le dîner]] is **lunch**. More on that below.

blocks.title: Every food has a gender
blocks.body:
You already know that French nouns are **masculine** or **feminine**. Food is no exception, and there is usually no logic to it: [[le fromage]] is masculine, [[la viande]] is feminine.

So always learn a food word **with its article**: not just *pain*, but [[le pain]]. Remember: [[le]] and [[la]] become [[l']] before a vowel ([[l'eau]]), and [[les]] is the plural for both genders.

blocks.note: Watch out: [[l'eau]] is feminine, [[les légumes]] is masculine, and [[les pâtes]] is feminine and always plural. You will practise [[le riz]], [[la pomme]], [[le thé]], [[le lait]] and [[le jus d'orange]] again in the next lesson.

blocks.title: Saying what you like
blocks.pattern: j'aime / je n'aime pas + le / la / l' / les + food
blocks.note:
English says “I like cheese” with no article. French **always** puts the definite article after [[aimer]]: [[J'aime le fromage]]. Here [[le]] means “cheese in general”.

To say you don't like something, wrap the verb in **ne … pas**: [[je n'aime pas]]. The [[ne]] becomes [[n']] before a vowel. The article after it does **not** change.

examples.en: Do you like pasta? (to a friend)

examples.fr: J'aime le café, mais pas le thé.
examples.en: I like coffee, but not tea.

blocks.title: Déjeuner, dîner, souper in Québec
blocks.body:
In Québec (and in much of French-speaking Canada, Belgium and Switzerland), the meal names keep their older meaning:

- [[le déjeuner]] = breakfast
- [[le dîner]] = lunch, around noon
- [[le souper]] = dinner, the evening meal

In France, it is [[le petit-déjeuner]], [[le déjeuner]] and [[le dîner]]. Everyone understands [[le petit-déjeuner]], but if a colleague in Montréal says “On dîne à midi ?”, they mean **lunch**.

You will also hear [[un breuvage]] in Québec for “a drink”: restaurant menus often have a *Breuvages* section. In France, the word is [[une boisson]].

examples.fr: Le souper, c'est à dix-huit heures.

blocks.body:
- **No article:** [[J'aime fromage]] is wrong. Say [[J'aime le fromage]].
- **Countable things go plural:** for things you count, like apples, use the plural to talk about them in general: [[J'aime les pommes]] (I like apples).
- **Wrong gender after a vowel:** you cannot hear the gender in [[l'eau]], so learn it: [[l'eau]] is feminine ([[une eau minérale]], a mineral water).
- **Forgetting ne:** in writing, [[je n'aime pas]] needs both parts. In fast speech, people often drop the [[ne]] ([[j'aime pas]]), but write it.

Lots of food words end in a **silent letter**:

- [[le riz]]: the z is silent, say “ree”.
- [[le lait]]: the t is silent, it rhymes with *est*.
- [[le poulet]]: “poo-leh”, no t.
- [[l'eau]]: just the sound “o”, with an l in front.

And [[le pain]] ends in a **nasal vowel**: let the air go through your nose and don't pronounce the n.

examples.fr: le riz, le lait, le poulet

[[Je n'aime pas]]: ne becomes n' before the vowel of aime. Keep the article: [[le poisson]].

accept: Est-ce que tu aimes le café ?
blocks.explain: [[tu aimes]] + [[le café]]. Raising your voice at the end makes it a question.
In general, with countable things, use the plural: [[les pommes]].

blocks.prompt: A colleague in Montréal says: “On dîne à midi ?” What is she suggesting?
blocks.explain: In Québec, [[dîner]] is the noon meal: lunch. In France, it would be the evening meal.
Remember the apostrophe in [[n'aime]] and the feminine article [[la viande]].

blocks.text: Le dîner, c'est à ___ heures. (19 h)
blocks.explain: 19 h = [[dix-neuf heures]]. French uses the 24-hour clock for times like this. In Québec, the evening meal would be [[le souper]].

blocks.prompt: Lucie asks you what you like for the welcome lunch. Say two foods you like, one food you don't like, and a drink you like. Then ask her a question.
checklist: A question: Et toi ? / Tu aimes… ?

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Moi, j'aime le poulet et les légumes. Je n'aime pas le fromage. J'aime beaucoup le thé. Et toi, Lucie, tu aimes le thé ?
models.en: I like chicken and vegetables. I don't like cheese. I really like tea. And you, Lucie, do you like tea?

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to Lucie for the welcome lunch: what you like, what you don't like, and what time you have lunch.
checklist: Two or three foods you like, with the right article
One thing you don't like (ne… pas)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour Lucie ! J'aime le poisson, le riz et les fruits. Je n'aime pas les pâtes. J'aime le café, mais pas le thé. Je mange à midi et demi. Merci !
models.en: Hi Lucie! I like fish, rice and fruit. I don't like pasta. I like coffee, but not tea. I eat at half past twelve. Thanks!

summary:
- Name common foods and drinks **with their article**: [[le pain, la viande, l'eau, les légumes]]…
- Say what you like and don't like: [[J'aime le fromage. Je n'aime pas le poisson.]]
- Name the meals in France ([[le petit-déjeuner, le déjeuner, le dîner]]) and in Québec ([[le déjeuner, le dîner, le souper]])
